claim: After the TLD name server for .com responds with the names of the four Route 53 name servers for example.com, the DNS resolver caches them, and the next time someone browses to example.com the resolver skips steps 3 and 4 (the root and TLD name servers). The name servers are typically cached for two days.

evidence.quote: The DNS resolver caches (stores) the four Route 53 name servers. The next time someone browses to example.com, the resolver skips steps 3 and 4 because it already has the name servers for example.com. The name servers are typically cached for two days.
The DNS resolver for the ISP forwards the request for www.example.com to a DNS root name server.

The DNS resolver forwards the request for www.example.com again, this time to one of the TLD name servers for .com domains. The name server for .com domains responds with the names of the four Route 53 name servers associated with the example.com domain.
